title: Exceptional transport object and functor data
statement: Given the finite and integral operation families and compact-support left realizations of the exceptional ring construction, there exists the object, functor, adjunction, reconstruction, evaluation, and integral-left-realization data fields of an ExceptionalIntegralScalar.Transported record.

source.place: Constructions 4.1 and 5.25, Lemma 5.22 and Propositions 5.24 and 5.26

proof.text: Choose the reconstruction and shift package from the isolated reconstruction subproblem. Choose coherent integral operations and realizations from the integral compactification realization theorem. Apply the isolated transported functor/comparison package and assemble the independent fields of TransportCoreData. Define reductionF and reductionG from realizeF and realizeG by whiskering through the target reconstruction functor and composing with its counit isomorphism and the right unitor; do not choose the two reduction comparisons independently.

proof_origin.place: Constructions 4.1 and 5.25, Lemma 5.22 and Proposition 5.26; component formulas for functor whiskering

lean.statement:
theorem exists_exceptional_transport_core_data
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra (Padic l) Ω]
    [IsAlgClosure (Padic l) Ω] (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (c : Compactification f)
    (operation : ∀ s : RingStage.{u} l, Operation.{u} l Ω X Y (s.stage l))
    (left : ∀ s : RingStage.{u} l,
      LeftRealization.{u} l Ω c s (operation s)) :
    Nonempty (TransportCoreData l Ω D hl c operation left)
lean.note: The reduction comparison names and types are preserved; they are now canonical definitions from realizeF/realizeG and the reconstruction counits, rather than independent record fields.
